sections.heading: The reviewed case and its status
paragraphs: The FTC filed its complaint against Premier Franchising Group, the Premier Martial Arts franchisor, and former sales organisation Franchise Fastlane on 5 October 2026 in Eastern District of Tennessee case 3:26-cv-00487.

At the 12 November 2026 Pacific-time review, the FTC index, last updated 13 October, said Pending. Both posted stipulated orders had blank judicial signature/date fields. They contain non-admission language; court entry and a later disposition were not independently verified.

sections.heading: Would the newcomer do the same work as the reference owner?
paragraphs: In paragraphs 134–150, the FTC alleges the sellers promoted profitable semi-absentee ownership to buyers without martial-arts experience, often claiming fewer than 15 hours a week from the beginning, without evidence supporting that result for those operators.

The complaint contrasts established, often larger Legacy studios run by experienced owners with the smaller-studio newcomer model. It alleges differences in obligations, curriculum freedom and fees, selective inclusion of results and combined multi-studio figures presented as a single studio.

Paragraph 118 reports a 2022 FDD comparison of average 2021 EBITDA: $75,950 for the combined studio group versus $17,584 for New Franchisee studios. The first figure is not Legacy-only. EBITDA means earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation; it is not cash available to the owner. These are complaint-reported figures, not verified accounts or a forecast.

sections.heading: The same comparison matters in calls and sales material
paragraphs: The FTC also alleges break-even and studio-earnings claims appeared outside the relevant Item 19 disclosures, and that Item 2 omitted Franchise Fastlane personnel despite their franchise-sales management responsibilities. For a brand making its own comparison, include the owner’s teaching, selling, absence cover and difficult decisions, not just a manager’s salary. Item 19 has required disclosures even without an elected earnings claim; a claim needs its reasonable basis, written support, relevant historical groups or forecast assumptions and qualifications. Item 2 concerns people with relevant sale/operation management responsibility and their last five years of principal positions and employers. An outside broker’s actual role matters; this case does not give every broker Franchise Fastlane’s alleged role.

sections.heading: What the proposed orders do not establish
paragraphs: The proposals address income/sales, break-even time, owner hours, semi-absentee claims and Franchise Rule compliance. Premier Franchising Group’s proposed cancellation-notice mechanism covers a defined group and excludes Legacy Franchisees, certain settling claimants and transferees.

Those proposed terms do not establish a present right to cancel, an entered monetary obligation, a refund, payment or a delivered notice. The actual entered record and eligibility would be needed for that conclusion.

rows: An Alaska personal-income-tax withholding conclusion was not established in this review. Do not infer the absence of other employee deductions or payroll obligations.

TaxWeb registers new businesses; the agency handbook requires UI accounts for workers hired and working in Alaska and says workers brought from elsewhere may also need reporting. The registration requests entity type and first wage date.

bullets: The retrieved handbook says last updated April 2024. This review uses its account/localization instructions, not annual contribution rates or a complete current exemption determination.

sections.heading: Arizona
paragraphs: A company that already holds an Arizona withholding account still needs the UI application route. Track each agency's determination instead of treating the joint form as a single approval.

rows: DES identifies the Joint Tax Application JT-1/UC-001 and an existing-withholding-account route, but the separate DOR withholding-obligations page returned HTTP 403. Withholding liability and sourcing remain unresolved.

Submit JT-1/UC-001 through DOR; DES uses it to decide UI liability and separately issues a determination stating the coverage start date, rate and eight-digit account number. The EIN is required for processing.

bullets: This records the DES process and separate review, not a conclusion that every Arizona business owes UI or withholding. DOR substantive withholding access remains blocked.

sections.heading: Arkansas
paragraphs: Do not substitute a federal UI threshold for Arkansas's stated ten-day ordinary-employer test. Assemble paid-work days, first wage date, ownership and acquisition facts before the Tax 21 session, which the agency says has no save option.

rows: The 2026 DFA instructions require withholding registration through AR-1R and identify ATAP online registration. They distinguish work in Arkansas from work outside it and allocate nonresident partly in-state services to Arkansas workdays.

The Reemployment agency uses Tax 21 and describes ordinary employer status after one or more workers perform services on ten or more days in a calendar year, plus acquisition, domestic, agricultural and voluntary-coverage categories.

bullets: Special employer categories have separate tests; the ten-day statement is not a universal threshold. The withholding PDF's employment-verification statements were not relied upon for federal I-9 rules.

sections.heading: California
paragraphs: Enroll the portal user, verify the email within EDD's stated 24-hour window, then submit the separate New Employer application. Preserve the eight-digit payroll account number; user enrollment alone does not create it.

rows: EDD registers employer payroll tax accounts through e-Services for Business and supplies distinct commercial, household, agricultural, nonprofit and other forms. Select the correct account category rather than treating incorporation as payroll enrollment.

EDD Step 1 requires a business that hires employees and pays more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter to register within 15 days. Household employment has a separate $750 cash-wage threshold; use the appropriate account category.

bullets: Annual tax rates, wage bases, excluded employment, disability and paid-leave contributions require their own current review. Registration does not resolve worker classification.

sections.heading: Colorado
paragraphs: A foreign or other out-of-state employer should follow the CR 0100 branch rather than assuming the in-state portal route applies. Assign a separate owner to resolve CDLE unemployment registration.

rows: DOR requires a withholding-agent account when Colorado withholding is required. Its instructions distinguish in-state businesses using MyBizColorado or CR 0100 from out-of-state businesses using CR 0100; the account has no fee or renewal requirement.
The attempted CDLE registration page returned HTTP 403. The UI account procedure, liability thresholds and multi-state allocation were not substantively verified.

bullets: This establishes a conditional withholding-account process, not the underlying wage sourcing test, UI clearance or freedom from local occupational/payroll taxes.

sections.heading: Connecticut
paragraphs: Record both legal entity type and tax election before deciding whether an owner-manager's remuneration belongs in UI reports. An S corporation's federal income-tax treatment does not by itself exempt its paid officer's services from Connecticut UI.

rows: DRS links withholding to maintaining an office or transacting business in Connecticut and federal employer status, regardless of payroll department location. Register through myconneCT or add withholding to an existing DRS account.

DOL requires online ReEmployCT registration for employers of one or more people and separately describes liability thresholds. It expressly distinguishes sole proprietors, partners, paid corporate officers and LLC members according to relevant tax filing treatment.

bullets: The agency's LLC/officer discussion is Connecticut-specific. Family, nonprofit, domestic and other special coverage conditions still need fact-specific review.

sections.heading: Delaware
paragraphs: Map the employee's residence and actual work location before choosing full employer registration or withholding-agent-only treatment. Keep UC-1 submission and the resulting liability decision with the payroll file.

rows: One Stop distinguishes an employer conducting business in Delaware from an out-of-state business that may register as a withholding agent only for a Delaware resident as a courtesy. Do not turn that optional resident-service route into a universal duty.

One Stop directs businesses hiring one or more employees in Delaware to file UC-1 to determine unemployment liability and identifies withholding and workers' compensation as separate employer workstreams.

bullets: Only agency routing and the residence/work distinction were relied upon; older form names and broad withholding language on One Stop were not treated as complete current computation guidance.

sections.heading: Florida
paragraphs: Classify a service business as general, domestic, agricultural or another category before applying a threshold. Preserve the DR-1 determination; the guide treats corporate officers and LLC members differently according to the stated facts and tax classification.

rows: DOR expressly states Florida does not impose personal income tax. This closes only the state personal wage-income withholding branch; reemployment tax, corporate tax, sales tax and other payroll/business obligations remain separate.

DOR's reemployment guide requires DR-1 to determine liability; quarterly reports alone do not register an employer. It states general $1,500 quarterly wages, one employee in 20 weeks, or federal unemployment-tax liability tests, with separate special-employer categories.

bullets: The reemployment guide is revised March 2025; its annual rates were not relied on. The separate DOR tax guide supports the table’s narrow personal-income-tax statement. Worker classification and a complete current exclusion review remain outside this record.

sections.heading: Georgia
paragraphs: Put the first Georgia payroll date on the launch calendar and assign DOL-1A immediately afterwards. Keep payroll withholding and nonresident owner/distribution withholding as separate finance questions.

rows: DOR identifies employee-wage withholding, a separate registration-for-withholding-number route and Form G-4. Its page also covers other payment types, so a payroll number is not a determination of every nonresident-payment duty.

GDOL directs employing units with people performing services in Georgia to submit DOL-1A immediately after the first Georgia payroll. The FAQ separately states general liability and domestic/agricultural tests.

bullets: The DOR page contains a general rate description and the UI FAQ contains older wage-base text; neither was relied on as current rates or wage bases.

sections.heading: Hawaii
paragraphs: A Hawaii-based company sending staff outside the state cannot assume all wage withholding disappears. For UI, establish the owner's authorized account first and delegate the payroll provider through agency permissions.

rows: DOTAX states withholding applies to services in Hawaii and specified services outside it linked to the regular workplace or paying office. Obtain the WH account using BB-1 or add it in Hawaii Tax Online; the account has no opening fee.

The UI agency generally links tax to employees working in Hawaii and requires business owners to create the employer profile, after which they may authorize staff or service companies. Nonprofit, family-corporation and successor elections have separate conditions.

bullets: The withholding page contains inconsistent older return-form guidance; only its account and sourcing sections support this entry. Special UI elections are applications, not automatic exclusions.

sections.heading: Idaho
paragraphs: If a sole proprietorship becomes an LLC or a foreign buyer acquires operations, check the new-account branch. Using the predecessor's withholding voucher does not establish the buyer's own account.

rows: Obtain the EIN first, then use Idaho Business Registration. The Tax Commission says a withholding account is not transferable and requires a new account on business acquisition, a new EIN or a change of entity.

The Tax Commission's IBR guide routes businesses with employees to income-tax withholding and employee-related permits from Labor and the Industrial Commission. Prepare expected employee count, first paycheck and hire dates.

bullets: The separate UI handbook URL returned 404; IBR routing is verified, but Labor's substantive UI liability thresholds and localization are unresolved.

sections.heading: Illinois
paragraphs: Include a startup date and any purchase/reorganization in the payroll brief. The same portal can serve both agencies, but withholding registration and UI succession are different determinations.

rows: IDOR requires registration when Illinois withholding is mandatory or voluntarily undertaken and asks when Illinois payroll begins. MyTax Illinois/REG-1 handles registration; household employment has separate guidance.

IDES directs newly created employing units to register within 30 days of startup through MyTax Illinois or the liability form. A merger, acquisition or entity change has a separate succession/update workstream.

bullets: The 30-day statement is the agency's employing-unit registration rule, not a conclusion about every entity's tax liability. No current rate or full reciprocal-state analysis was performed.

sections.heading: Indiana
paragraphs: Record the actual Indiana work location and county before payroll setup. Creating an ESS user and obtaining the employer SUTA account are separate steps; use the agent route for a payroll provider.

rows: DOR directs employee businesses to collect state and county wage withholding, obtain an EIN and register through INBiz. It expressly points to county-specific rates rather than one statewide payroll setting.
DWD's Uplink ESS registration requires FEIN, legal name, NAICS, Indiana work location, first payroll date and responsible-party details; the SUTA number follows completed and approved registration.

bullets: This records account inputs and the existence of county withholding. It does not select an employee's county rate, settle reciprocity or verify every UI coverage exception.

sections.heading: Iowa
paragraphs: Treat a remote Iowa hire by a foreign or other out-of-state employer as a distinct registration event. Use a properly authorized agent account, not shared employer credentials, and confirm the applicable multi-state allocation before reporting.

rows: IDR links withholding to an office or business in Iowa, federal withholding and services performed in Iowa; obtain FEIN before Iowa registration. Residence and multi-state services still require the applicable sourcing review.

IWD says register through myIowaUI within 30 days of first Iowa wages or acquisition; out-of-state employers must register as soon as Iowa wages are paid. It separately discusses base-of-operations and direction/control for multi-state workers.

bullets: The agency page has a 2026 note changing out-of-state wage credits alongside older text; no wage-credit amount is asserted here. Account routing is not full employment-law coverage.

sections.heading: Kansas
paragraphs: Do not put a Kansas client's payroll under the reporting agent's own tax number. Identify resident versus nonresident workers and distinguish the employer's wage account from any owner-payment withholding.

rows: KDOR's KW-100 directs covered employers/payers to register through its Customer Service Center and separately addresses Kansas-resident and Kansas-work wages. It distinguishes wage withholding from nonresident-owner accounts and reporting-agent accounts.
The KDOL employer-services page returned HTTP 403; the current UI account route, timing and liability test were not substantively verified.

bullets: KW-100 displays revision 24.08. Its registration and account distinctions were reviewed, not current rates or a comprehensive 2026 wage-sourcing exception inventory.

sections.heading: Kentucky
paragraphs: Budget access to MyTaxes before payroll rather than assuming a paper-payment route. Assign a separate UI registration check and a local occupational-tax review for the employee's actual locality.

rows: DOR identifies resident/nonresident wage withholding subject to exemptions and directs registration, filing and payment through MyTaxes. Its 2026 instructions require electronic filing/payment for all employer filing frequencies.

The official employer page routes liable employers to an Employer Reserve Account, including acquisitions. The January 2026 KUIP FAQ says an account number and report filing are available immediately after completed registration.

bullets: The attempted UI-1 link returned non-substantive content; the separate official employer page and January 2026 KUIP FAQ were read. Liability thresholds, local occupational taxes and current rates remain separate.

sections.heading: Louisiana
paragraphs: Time account activation to the actual withholding start rather than opening it speculatively. Separately determine whether LAWATS needs a new employer account or access to an existing account, and preserve the agency's resulting status.

rows: LDR requires a withholding account before filing/remitting, but specifically warns not to register until Louisiana wage withholding begins. LaTAP registers a new business or adds an account; Secretary of State registration and EIN do not create it.

LWC's LAWATS login instructions require an existing seven-digit Employer Account Number and FEIN; a business without the EAN must apply for the unemployment tax account first. The owner then grants a third-party administrator access.

bullets: The LAWATS login guide is dated April 11, 2024. It distinguishes portal access from the tax account but does not establish current UI liability thresholds or sourcing exemptions.

sections.heading: Maine
paragraphs: A New Hampshire employer with a Maine resident should document work and business-location facts, not infer Maine withholding solely from residence or solely from headquarters. Preserve the distinction between mandatory and courtesy withholding.

rows: MRS's April 2026 FAQ routes new withholding accounts through the Maine Tax Portal and separately tests an out-of-state employer's Maine office/business, taxable payments and federal withholding. Courtesy withholding can differ from mandatory withholding.

The official ReEmployME guide distinguishes registration of a business without an EAN from creating access to an existing account. It states general and separate nonprofit/agricultural coverage tests and says a future date cannot be used to set up an account.

bullets: Official www1.maine.gov mirrors supplied the MRS FAQ and ReEmployME system guide after the main host blocked access. No annual rate, complete UI exclusion list or full remote-work sourcing determination is supplied.

sections.heading: Maryland
paragraphs: Record remuneration to a paid officer and the actual employing entity before labeling a small company 'owner only.' After BEACON, obtain a separate Comptroller withholding answer rather than treating UI enrollment as all tax registration.

rows: The 2026 Comptroller guide requires CRA registration and a Central Registration Number, warns not to wait until withholding is due, and says an acquirer must not use the seller's number. The September 2026 CRA guide routes applications through Maryland Tax Connect.

Labor requires an employer UI account through BEACON, distinguishes covered from excluded work and expressly includes paid corporate officers in covered employment. Other tax registration and UI are separate.

bullets: Withholding and UI registration are separate from Maryland FAMLI, local withholding computations, worker exclusions and full wage sourcing. No annual rate or paid-leave date is asserted.

sections.heading: Massachusetts
paragraphs: A short Massachusetts assignment by an out-of-state company deserves its own UI review; do not automatically substitute a familiar $1,500 threshold from another category or state. Distinguish proprietor income from wages to an employee.

rows: DOR's August 2026 guide distinguishes resident and nonresident wages and directs employers to register before filing/payment through MassTaxConnect. A sole proprietor is generally not an employee solely for paying their own personal tax.

DUA lists general contribution tests and distinct domestic/agricultural categories; it specifically states an out-of-state employer test of $200 gross Massachusetts wages in a quarter. Its account route is Unemployment Services for Employers.

bullets: The $200 statement is the agency's out-of-state-employer category, not a universal tax-free allowance or a withholding threshold. No annual rates or full sourcing exceptions are supplied.

sections.heading: Michigan
paragraphs: Confirm the current MiUI workflow rather than reusing an old payroll-provider checklist. Keep the employer's own access and authorize the third party through the agency route; a provider's login is not the employer's registration evidence.

rows: Treasury's MTO business-tax eRegistration process and separate user/business-account linkage were read, but that general page does not establish withholding liability, sourcing or account-selection criteria. Those remain unresolved.

UIA's current help center says MiUI is live for all tax/benefit functions and employers should hold their own MiUI account even when using a third-party administrator. It separately routes business registration and account authorization.

bullets: The reviewed Treasury page covers business registration generally; withholding liability and sourcing require a separate substantive tax analysis. No broad Michigan tax clearance is implied.

sections.heading: Minnesota
paragraphs: Minnesota's withholding and UI account timing differ: prepare withholding before deductions, but do not preregister UI before covered wages are actually paid. Retain both numbers and resolve owner/officer coverage before selecting wage records.

rows: DOR's new-employer guide requires a Minnesota ID and withholding account before tax is withheld. It distinguishes that number from DEED's UI account used for state unemployment reporting.

The UI handbook says register after covered wages have actually been paid and before the first required quarterly wage-detail report is due. It asks entity type, owner/officer interests, Minnesota work dates and acquisition facts, with special categories treated separately.

bullets: Covered employment, owner/officer elections, nonprofit and other special categories still require their own tests. This is not a Paid Leave registration or full employment-law determination.

sections.heading: Mississippi
paragraphs: A recruitment-platform registration does not activate unemployment reporting. For an acquisition, tell DOR the ownership/entity facts and retain the correct acquiring-employer account before the first post-acquisition payroll.

rows: DOR requires a withholding account for employers subject to Mississippi withholding, with online application through TAP. Its instructions require acquisition/entity changes to be assessed rather than using the predecessor's addressed return.

MDES separates employment-service registration from the New Business unemployment-tax registration, and separately offers online access for an already assigned account. An employer needing both service categories must register for both.

bullets: This does not establish UI liability thresholds or all resident/nonresident sourcing rules. No annual withholding/UI rate is supplied.

sections.heading: Missouri
paragraphs: Keep the legal entity filing, DOR withholding number and UI liability outcome as three records. A foreign company temporarily sending a team should also investigate the transient-employer category before assuming ordinary registration is sufficient.

rows: DOR's 2026 guide directs employers paying wages to employees working in Missouri to register online or using Form 2643. The permanent withholding number is not transferable; transient-employer requirements are a separate category.

Labor's new-employer guide distinguishes Secretary of State formation from DOR tax registration and directs the employer to a separate UI liability review. New liable employers receive an industrial classification for UI.

bullets: The Labor checklist is an official route to the separate liability process, not a complete UI threshold finding. Transient-employer security amounts and exemptions remain unresolved.

sections.heading: Montana
paragraphs: A zero-withholding W-2 does not by itself remove the account question described by Montana DOR. Put the Montana work-start date and the legal employer's IRS-matching name into the application brief.

rows: DOR requires a withholding account when a business issues Montana wages, W-2s with or without withholding, or 1099s with withholding. Apply through TAP or GenReg with FEIN and the date employees started Montana work.

DLI's UI eServices is the named employer registration/reporting portal, with separate UI Contributions Bureau assistance. The page establishes the account route, not the coverage or localization test.

bullets: No UI threshold, worker exclusion, tax rate or multi-state allocation is established by the portal overview. Other state payroll deductions remain separate.

sections.heading: Nebraska
paragraphs: Obtain the employer's own withholding certificate before the provider files. At the year change, use the correctly dated Circular EN: the official page separates tables through December 31, 2026 from those starting January 1, 2027.

rows: DOR requires Form 20 and a Nebraska withholding number before state deductions. The employer remains responsible for the application when using a payroll service; provide that service the issued Withholding Certificate.

Nebraska One Stop identifies the DOL unemployment tax-account application, but its short listing supplies no thresholds or complete instructions. Substantive coverage and registration inputs remain open.

bullets: The FAQ retains older rate and pandemic passages; those are not relied on. Current numeric rates and UI liability are not established here.

sections.heading: Nevada
paragraphs: Do not substitute another state's $1,500 general threshold for Nevada's stated $225 test. Record the Nevada work and wage facts and request the actual account/coverage decision, including any excluded-employment question.

rows: Nevada Constitution Article 10,section 1(9) prohibits income tax on natural persons' wages/personal income while permitting business-income/revenue taxes. Personal wage-income withholding is therefore distinct from UI, Modified Business Tax and other business taxes.

DETR says generally an employing unit paying $225 or more for Nevada employment in a calendar quarter must register with Employment Security and pay UI tax. Its employing-unit definition includes entities and individuals.

bullets: The $225 statement is a general UI coverage rule, not a tax-free allowance or an MBT/other-tax conclusion. Annual rates and all exceptions were not reviewed.

sections.heading: New Hampshire
paragraphs: A transfer of a New Hampshire workforce is itself a reporting event. Assemble predecessor, assets, trade/workforce and entity details rather than limiting the registration brief to the first wage amount.

rows: NH Economy's state economic-development guidance states there is no state income tax in its salary/cost-of-living context. This is limited to personal wage-income withholding; business-profits and business-enterprise taxes and other employer duties remain separate.

Emp 303.01, amended effective June 26, 2026, requires an Employer Status Report within 30 days of furnishing employment, becoming an employer, specified status changes or business/workforce transfers. It requests entity, NH work and wage dates, locations and acquisition facts.

bullets: The operative current rule was read from the official administrative-code text; the NHES agency handbook download was blocked. Portal steps, underlying statutory coverage and all exceptions need separate confirmation.

sections.heading: New Jersey
paragraphs: For a Pennsylvania resident, retain the required reciprocity certificate rather than assuming residence alone stops NJ withholding. Separately evaluate UI and other contributions; an income-tax reciprocal rule does not settle those duties or Pennsylvania local wage taxes.

rows: NJ-WT requires FEIN and, for a corporate entity, the state's ten-digit corporate ID for registration. It distinguishes resident/nonresident work, Pennsylvania reciprocity certificates and certain convenience-of-employer sourcing.

Employer Accounts directs NJ-REG first and describes employer status after one or more workers and $1,000 annual wages, with automatic coverage for FUTA-subject employing units. UI, disability and family-leave contributions are named separately.

bullets: NJ-WT is marked September 2025. No full convenience-rule, reciprocity, worker-classification or annual-rate determination is made. Historical case excerpts on the UI page are not treated as independently reviewed court decisions.

sections.heading: New Mexico
paragraphs: Do not treat payment of the workers' compensation administrative fee as an insurance policy: TRD expressly distinguishes them. Obtain separate UI and insurance evidence as well as the wage-withholding account.

rows: TRD requires employer registration to file wage withholding and describes resident/out-of-state-work and nonresident/in-state-work definitions with limited exceptions. It distinguishes wage from non-wage withholding and the workers' compensation administrative fee.
TRD routes UI to Workforce Solutions, but the attempted DWS pages and handbook returned a short challenge response rather than substantive text. UI registration and coverage remain unresolved.

bullets: No UI liability finding, full nonresident exception analysis, insurance premium or current fee computation is provided.

sections.heading: New York
paragraphs: Assign the employer's registration separately from a PEO or payroll representative's access. Verify the correct employing entity and program enrollment even when combined returns and payments are handled in one dashboard.

rows: NYS-50 identifies online registration or NYS-100 for the combined withholding, wage-reporting and UI program, with separate forms for some employer types. An existing entity filing is not that payroll registration.

NYSDOL says liable employers pay into the fund through Tax and Finance but must register with Labor. Its current system separately manages employer, PEO and third-party representative accounts; UI contributions cannot be deducted from employees.

bullets: The current DOL page redirects to the upgraded system. No full UI liability, New York City/Yonkers, convenience-rule, paid-leave or wage-sourcing determination is made.

sections.heading: North Carolina
paragraphs: Separate employee wage withholding from fees to a nonresident contractor or owner. Record the NCSUITS liability result rather than applying the general business threshold to domestic, nonprofit, agricultural or acquired operations.

rows: NCDOR directs payroll withholding applicants to NC-BR and distinguishes wage from nonwage accounts. Its FAQ notes a possible account exception when employees' state withholding certificates mean no wage withholding is required.

DES states general $1,500-quarter/20-week tests and separate employer categories, acquisitions and FUTA coverage. NCSUITS registration yields an Employer ID and liability status, followed by a liability-date/rate letter.

bullets: The withholding-certificate note is not a general exemption from payroll registration. Nonwage sourcing, worker classification and all UI exceptions remain separate.

sections.heading: North Dakota
paragraphs: A saved draft or entered business data is not an agency receipt: retain the UI EASY confirmation after certification/submission. Assign a separate new-employer coverage check and collect employee work/residence facts before selecting deductions.

rows: The Tax Commissioner directs employers to register an income-tax withholding account through ND TAP, and distinguishes exemptions and wage-return filing. The account process does not itself resolve resident/nonresident or reciprocal-state treatment.

Job Service's UI EASY page establishes reporting/payment and account-access functions and requires certified submission to obtain a receipt. The new-employer application and substantive liability criteria were not established by that overview.

bullets: No UI coverage threshold or complete reciprocal-state/withholding exemption inventory is asserted.

sections.heading: Ohio
paragraphs: A remote Ohio hire requires checking the actual work location and employee's taxing school district. Do not treat state withholding as city-tax or UI clearance, and confirm the current JFS route independently.

rows: The 2026 DOR guide directs qualifying employers with Ohio work, including remote work, to register through OH|TAX eServices using an FEIN. It separately identifies resident school-district withholding, using the employer's same withholding account.

The DOR guide identifies JFS unemployment-tax reporting as a separate workstream, but the attempted JFS new-employer pages returned 404. The current UI application, liability and timing remain unresolved.

bullets: The official CDN supplied the 2026 PDF while the attempted public HTML routes failed. No school-district rate, municipal withholding, full reciprocity or UI exemption is determined.

sections.heading: Oklahoma
paragraphs: Check which OESC system currently handles the required action and retain the employer's account confirmation. Distinguish ordinary business from domestic, agricultural and nonprofit categories before applying the general test.

rows: OTC identifies employee-wage withholding and directs filing/payment through OkTAP; the New Business Center separately routes applications for required tax accounts. The reviewed pages do not resolve this employer's sourcing or exemption facts.

OESC states general $1,500-quarter or one-worker/20-week contribution tests, with special categories. It explains a phased transition between EZ Tax and the new Employer Portal rather than implying every function is already in the new portal.

bullets: OkTAP filing and the tax-account application route are identified; underlying wage sourcing, exemptions, acquisition effects and special UI categories still require review.

sections.heading: Oregon
paragraphs: Obtain the payroll BIN rather than confusing it with the Secretary of State business number. Include corporate-officer compensation and the exact work/transport-district locations; identify each applicable program even though reporting is combined.

rows: DOR directs paid-employee employers to obtain a BIN before issuing paychecks using Revenue Online or Combined Employer's Registration. It also addresses corporations reporting officer compensation and says a structure change can require a new BIN.

Oregon's Combined Payroll Tax Reporting System uses the BIN for withholding, unemployment and named additional payroll programs. The common identifier does not make every program's wage or coverage test identical.

bullets: Transit taxes, Workers' Benefit Fund, paid leave and excluded employment require their own applicability analysis. Portal processing estimates are not an opening guarantee.

sections.heading: Pennsylvania
paragraphs: A Pennsylvania home-based employee can create a payroll workstream for an out-of-state business. Record both work and residence municipality/county and find the competent local tax collector; a state account does not settle local withholding.

rows: The state Business One-Stop guidance for an out-of-state employer hiring a remote Pennsylvania employee requires employer-withholding and UC accounts through myPATH, and separately identifies local earned-income/services-tax administration.
The same official remote-hire guide routes unemployment-compensation registration through myPATH and keeps workers' compensation information and new-hire reporting as separate tasks.

bullets: This is the agency's remote-hire registration branch, not a universal local-tax rate, full UC liability test or workers' compensation coverage conclusion.

sections.heading: Rhode Island
paragraphs: Prepare BAR data before payroll, but do not mistake inability to obtain the UI number before the first wage date for an exemption. Confirm whether the worker's service is localized in Rhode Island rather than selecting a UI state solely from headquarters.

rows: Taxation's online business registration can establish an income-tax withholding account and an unemployment account. It distinguishes retail-permit registration fees from the listed payroll-account registrations.

DLT directs a BAR application and says the UI account number follows the first Rhode Island payroll/liability date. It separately addresses proprietor/partner-only businesses and the localization of multi-state work.

bullets: No current contribution rate, complete excluded-employment list or resolution of disability/job-development contributions is provided.

sections.heading: South Carolina
paragraphs: File for the agency's liability determination rather than treating the first employee as proof of a particular tax amount. Keep MyDORWAY withholding, SUITS and new-hire confirmations as distinct evidence.

rows: Business One Stop directs businesses to obtain an SCDOR employer withholding account through MyDORWAY and says there is no account-registration charge. It keeps withholding separate from unemployment and new-hire reporting.
The same official guide says a business with at least one employee must file with SCDEW, which determines UI liability or non-liability. The employer account route is SUITS.

bullets: The one-employee filing statement is not a universal contribution threshold. Wage sourcing, exemptions, rates and the guide's separate immigration/workers' compensation statements were not verified here.

sections.heading: South Dakota
paragraphs: A conversion from proprietor to partnership or corporation is a new registration question, even if the workers remain. For a travelling crew, ask DLR to apply the multi-state reporting rules to the work pattern rather than choosing solely by residence.

rows: DOR's July 2026 Tax Basics states South Dakota has no personal income tax. That narrow income-tax branch does not remove reemployment assistance, sales/use, municipal or other business obligations.

DLR requires registration of new/acquired businesses and new registration after entity or ownership changes. Most use Form 1; nonprofit and political-subdivision forms differ. General and special liability tests are separate from the registration instruction.

bullets: The agency's temporary/out-of-state overview uses a 90-day distinction; this review does not resolve its exact boundary or replace localization analysis. No annual rate or full exclusion list is asserted.

sections.heading: Tennessee
paragraphs: Check whether the company already has an account before creating a new one. If access is missing, use the existing-employer Letter ID process; the payroll provider should follow its own TPA branch.

rows: Tennessee Revenue expressly states it has no general personal income tax. That narrow personal wage-income branch does not remove UI or other state business/payroll duties; the cited FAQ is dated June 15, 2021.

TDLWD distinguishes existing employers signing up for e-Services using FEIN and a recent Letter ID from new employers choosing Register my business. PEOs and third-party administrators have separate identity/registration branches.

bullets: The UI source establishes account-access and application routes, not the underlying UI liability threshold or rules for assigning multi-state work. The separate Revenue FAQ supports the table’s narrow personal-income-tax statement.

sections.heading: Texas
paragraphs: Record the liability date separately from the first visit to UTR, and confirm the employer qualifies for online registration. Preserve the Employer Liability Notice; a saved UTR draft is not completed registration.

rows: Texas Constitution Article 8,section 24-a prohibits a tax on individuals' net incomes. This closes the personal wage-income withholding branch only; unemployment and Texas business/franchise or other taxes remain separate.

TWC requires registration within 10 days of becoming liable. UTR gathers ownership/payroll facts, determines liability and issues an account number to liable employers; some categories cannot register online. UTS is the later reporting/payment service.

bullets: No universal first-hire liability test or online eligibility list is established here. The stated 10-day deadline begins with liability, not automatically entity formation.

sections.heading: Utah
paragraphs: A foreign finance team should arrange an authorized application route early rather than repeatedly trying a geographically unavailable TAP service. Keep the tax-account application and DWS coverage/status record distinct.

rows: The Tax Commission directs an online TC-69 application through TAP to obtain the withholding number, then a separate TAP login. It warns that TAP is unavailable in most countries outside the U.S. and offers an agency contact.

DWS requires a Status Report/Form 1 for new or acquired businesses and after ownership/entity changes to determine coverage. Online registration issues initial account information, followed by status-examiner finalization.

bullets: The handbook contains broader benefits and historical material; only employer registration/change-of-entity sections support this entry. No UI rate, liability exception or special bond amount is asserted.

sections.heading: Vermont
paragraphs: Resolve Vermont wage taxability and the separate registration procedure before configuring payroll. Do not turn an inaccessible agency page into a no-registration conclusion; retain an assigned agency follow-up for both processes.

rows: 32 V.S.A. § 5841 links withholding to federal withholding and payments also subject to Vermont income tax. That statutory duty was read, but the Taxes Department account-registration pages returned 403; the application procedure remains unresolved.
The Labor registration page returned 403. The current UI registration application, account timing, liability and localization rules were not substantively verified.

bullets: The Legislature's online statute says it incorporates the 2026 session and is an unofficial convenience copy. Only the conditional withholding duty is established; no account process, rate or broad employment-law clearance.

sections.heading: Virginia
paragraphs: A home-based service company is not a household employer merely because its office is a house. Separately confirm the FC-27 coverage condition and retain the VEC number/rate notice; an early incomplete registration is not approval.

rows: Virginia Tax requires withholding registration, returns and payment for employers required to file. It distinguishes the household-employer annual option from business employees, including employees of a business operated from home.

paragraphs: The English translation ends its validity in 2024 and omits later amendments. The current Latvian statute and the named Cabinet provisions were read with AI-assisted English interpretation for this explanation.

title: Does selling to America settle the VAT on your foreign software purchase?

sections.heading: Know what your registration does
paragraphs: Article 10 is the ordinary VAT registration discussed here: VAT applies to taxable supplies taking place in Malta, while recovery of purchase VAT depends on the applicable credit rules. Article 11 is the domestic small-enterprise scheme for eligible Malta-established businesses; its exemption is without input-tax credit. Eligibility and turnover calculation are governed by the Sixth Schedule.

Article 12 deals with specified cross-border transactions. It can be required alongside Article 11: the Act expressly says an Article 11 business receiving services for which it must pay VAT must also register under Article 12. The domestic sales exemption is therefore not an exemption from every foreign purchase.

sections.heading: Check who must account for VAT on the foreign service
paragraphs: For the general business-services case in Article 20(2)(b), a taxable service received in Malta from a supplier not established there and not Article 10-registered can make the Maltese recipient liable for the tax. If you are a Malta-established taxable person outside Article 10 registration and receive a service for which Article 20(2) makes you liable, Article 12(3) requires registration by the date you receive it. For an Article 11 support business buying covered foreign cloud access, that purchase duty is separate from how its American sale is treated. Article 12 itself does not provide input-tax recovery.

sections.heading: For the sale, establish who receives your service
paragraphs: The VAT Act’s Third Schedule item 2(a) generally follows the business customer or the fixed establishment receiving the service, subject to exceptions. MTCA’s American-buyer example accepts sufficient appropriate evidence that the customer purchases for its business even though it has no EU VAT number.

So the missing EU number does not automatically make your buyer a consumer. Establish its business purpose, the receiving establishment and the kind of service. An American address alone does not answer those questions. In the cloud example, those facts decide the sale analysis; your own status and purchase liability decide the separate registration question.

sections.heading: The other-EU service branch has its own trigger
paragraphs: Article 12(3a) separately concerns a Malta-established taxable person outside Article 10 supplying services in another EU Member State for which the recipient alone pays VAT under Article 196. Registration is due by the date of that supply. An American customer is not that other Member State.

practicalOutput: Identify your actual registration and the foreign service’s place of supply and supplier status before receiving it; complete any required Article 12 registration by that date.
limitations: This explains the specified registration and service-liability rules, not a complete eligibility, turnover, credit, rate, invoice or VAT-return decision. learningSummary: Your domestic small-business VAT exemption does not necessarily cover VAT you must account for on foreign software. An Article 11 business can also need Article 12 registration for a covered foreign-service purchase, by the date it receives the service.

paragraphs: Current Article 12(1), point 2 describes services sold to a business that is neither domiciled in Iceland nor conducting business there from a fixed establishment. An American billing address does not establish both conditions. Other recipients have a separate point 3 route.

Ordinary support and work on an Icelandic building therefore need separate assessment. The point 2 exceptions include covered Icelandic property/accommodation, road access, local passenger transport, event and spa admission, catering, vehicle hire delivered to the lessee in Iceland, specified locally used telecom/broadcasting and travel services.

sections.heading: The recovered regulation still contains a conditional certificate rule
paragraphs: The official current PDF of Regulation 194/1990 labels its version in force from 9 September 2022 and the document 8 November 2026. Article 1 concerns its listed services to parties with neither residence nor a business place in Iceland. It gives alternatives: wholly used abroad, or the buyer could have deducted the VAT if its activity were Icelandically registered.

For that second, hypothetical-credit limb, the seller must request a home-country competent-authority certificate showing the buyer’s business. It is valid for two years from issue and retained like accounting records; the seller may seek two-year extensions where the basis is unchanged. That conditional wording is neither a certificate rule for every foreign invoice nor evidence that certificates have disappeared.

sections.heading: Do not turn either text into an unchecked invoice answer
paragraphs: The dates explain part of the mismatch: Act 63/2024 inserted the current business-recipient rule and separate non-business rule, and removed the former listed-service point. The official bill’s explanation describes a move from deciding actual use in Iceland to a general foreign-business recipient rule, subject to the named Icelandic-service exceptions. The older listed-service test is therefore not an adequate statement of the whole current statute.

That enactment does not, by itself, explain how every remaining condition in the current-hosted Regulation 194/1990 applies after the reform. The regulation still contains the conditional hypothetical-credit certificate rule described above, and the current Act still delegates power to set conditions. No later official instruction reconciling that certificate limb with the new business-recipient route was recovered. The regulation is not declared obsolete, and a certificate is not asserted for every U.S. invoice.

learningSummary: An American payer does not automatically make an Icelandic service an export. Check the statute’s actual foreign-business conditions and local-service exceptions. title: Ukraine: can branch funding pay for a separate U.S. company?
description: Why the recipient’s legal identity and payment purpose matter under the dated NBU sources, with older branch limits clearly separated from current payment approval.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Who receives the money matters
paragraphs: Suppose a Ukrainian company wants to fund a U.S. operation. First distinguish its own branch or representative office from a separately incorporated company. The branch provision in the older NBU control copy reviewed here expressly concerns foreign units without creating another legal entity, and exclusively their maintenance costs. It is not a general allowance to acquire ownership in another business.

Fictional example: a Ukrainian training brand forms a separate U.S. company and plans to send it startup capital. Calling that transfer “branch support” does not make the recipient a unit without a separate legal identity. The brand needs the current route for the actual investment payment, rather than assuming that an overseas-office allowance covers it.

sections.heading: What the older branch provision actually covered
paragraphs: The official NBU control copy recovered for this review has an amendment history ending on 13 January 2026. Its branch-maintenance provision contains cumulative conditions. The figures below explain that dated text; they have not been verified as the current allowance.
bullets: The Ukrainian resident legal entity must have operated for at least 12 months since state registration before the transfer. The recipient must be its own foreign branch, representative office or other unit without a separate legal entity.

The annual base is €1 million equivalent, calculated using the official NBU exchange rate on the transaction date. A further allowance uses documented 2021 maintenance transfers for qualifying units already open on 24 February 2022. The provision combines those amounts for the monthly calculation.

Transfers in one calendar month may not exceed one quarter of that combined annual amount. The payment must use the company’s own foreign currency, neither purchased nor raised through a credit or loan.

The company must use one chosen servicing bank; changing it follows the written procedure cross-referenced in the provision. Transfers are exclusively for maintenance costs, supported by an expense budget.

sections.heading: The NBU itself separates investment from other payments
paragraphs: In its explanation published on 26 August 2026, the NBU said there was no general permission for residents freely to invest abroad at that time. It separately discussed maintenance of foreign representative offices, current foreign-trade operations and export-contract penalties. Those categories should not be collapsed into a general permission to send expansion capital.

The same explanation described a mechanism for individual investments with economic or strategic justification serving state interests: the Ukrainian government may approach the NBU, which may consider a separate decision. It described this as exceptional, rather than a replacement for general currency liberalisation. An ordinary company should not treat it as a routine permission available merely on request.
That statement is dated. The complete current amended rule has not been reconciled here, so neither the statement nor the older numerical conditions establish eligibility for a present payment.

sections.heading: “IP payment” and “investment limit” are also incomplete descriptions
paragraphs: The older text has a separate provision for IP-protection fees and duties, foreign patent-office services and foreign patent-attorney services. That wording does not itself establish permission for a commercial royalty or the purchase of IP. Another provision links an allowance to qualifying foreign investment coming into the Ukrainian resident’s capital; its label does not make it a general permission to invest abroad.

Before promising that the Ukrainian company will fund the U.S. operation, identify the actual payer and recipient, their legal relationship, the payment’s purpose, the currency source and transaction date. The servicing bank needs the current applicable exception and conditions for those facts. A U.S. formation document, an old annual limit or a revised invoice description does not answer that question.

practicalOutput: Establish whether the transfer maintains the same company’s foreign unit or funds a separate business, then match that actual purpose to the current bank-payment route before committing the money.
limitations: The article explains dated primary documents. The full current Resolution 18 and complete 2026 amendment chain were not recovered; no current numerical allowance, service/IP payment approval or outward-equity clearance is claimed.
English explanations of Ukrainian sources are AI-assisted translations. Other currency rules, bank checks and the actual transaction remain separate.

learningSummary: A payment to maintain your company’s own overseas branch is different from investing in another company. The dated National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) documents reviewed here draw that distinction. Creating a U.S. company, or changing an invoice label, does not itself supply the Ukrainian outward-payment permission.

title: A contractor label does not decide the technician’s status
description: Equipment ownership and a signed contractor clause are not a complete employment test.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Is the person operating an independent business?
paragraphs: Relevant facts include who sets prices and schedules, accepts jobs, hires helpers, makes entrepreneurial investments, markets to other customers and has a genuine opportunity for profit or loss. Include actual practice and reserved rights.

In a fictional maintenance arrangement, the brand sets mandatory schedules and prices while the technician buys equipment. The contract says independent contractor, but says little about outside customers, helpers or profit and loss. Neither the label nor that purchase answers the whole question. Specialised skill alone does not establish an independent business.

sections.heading: The tax and wage questions are separate
paragraphs: The codified 29 CFR Part 795 interpretation reviewed in November 2026 examines the whole activity through six nonexclusive factors. No one factor or selected subset necessarily controls; it is not a points tally or a replacement for governing court law.

IRS employment-tax guidance instead groups common-law evidence into behavioural control, financial control and the type of relationship. It also considers the whole relationship; a right to control can matter even for remote work. A tax result or relief provision does not decide federal wage-and-hour duties under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) or state unemployment and wage law.

sections.heading: An investigation policy is not a repeal
paragraphs: The Department of Labor’s May 2025 bulletin changes its investigation approach within its stated scope and discretion; it expressly does not change employee rights or employer responsibilities. The named 2019 opinion was withdrawn in 2021 and expressly reissued, with its text reproduced, as FLSA2025-2 on May 2, 2025. That opinion concerns supplied virtual-marketplace facts, not automatic contractor treatment for technicians. The February 2026 replacement proposal, including its proposed expansion to the Family and Medical Leave Act and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act, is not effective merely because comments closed.

The cited Colt & Joe Trucking order concerned standing and stated alternative failed or waived arguments; it did not classify every technician. These source types cannot be used interchangeably to declare contractor treatment available.

A current court record supplies a narrower status answer: the Sixth Circuit’s 13 November 2026 pending-case report lists Littman v. Department of Labor, appeal 25-5335, as held in abeyance. That means the appeal is paused; it is not a ruling that the 2024 interpretation is valid or invalid. The November current code still contains Part 795, and the reviewed Federal Register record still labels its replacement a proposal. This does not establish the latest orders in every other challenge.

practicalOutput: Check the real control and independent-business facts before relying on contractor treatment in your staffing cost.
limitations: No worker, exemption, tax relief or state-law result is determined. The current governing test must be applied to the actual relationship.
learningSummary: Look at how the person actually earns money and works. Wage, tax and state tests can differ. The current code and proposal are checked, and a November 2026 court report confirms the Littman appeal is paused; neither that pause nor the contract label classifies your worker.
seoTitle: Worker classification: actual work and federal-source limits

title: Separate payroll does not always mean separate employer duties
description: The same worker can raise responsibilities for more than one business under the applicable law.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A real agency example: hours at two businesses
paragraphs: The Department of Labor’s Opinion Letter FLSA2025-05 considered a restaurant and members club with represented shared operations, managers and workers. On those supplied facts, it concluded the worker’s hours had to be combined and both employers were responsible for compliance with the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), the federal wage-and-hour law.

The letter is limited to the facts supplied and is not a court judgment about every franchise. Its practical lesson is to examine shared hours and real operations, rather than stop at the two payroll names.

sections.heading: An outcome inspection is different from setting a worker’s shift
paragraphs: Identify who selects workers, sets pay and individual schedules, directs performance, disciplines and terminates. A check of the contracted service outcome and an instruction about a named worker’s shift should not both be labelled quality control. Mixed-purpose controls and actual practice matter; neither fact alone completes a legal test.
Franchise classification asks about brand, operating control or assistance and payments. It does not itself decide who has duties to workers.

sections.heading: Which federal law is being applied?
paragraphs: For federal labour-relations law, the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA), the reviewed February 2026 final action restores the 2020 text: the 2023 rule never took effect after court vacatur. Substantial direct and immediate control over one or more listed essential employment terms is central; indirect or unexercised reserved authority has the rule’s qualified supplementary role.

For federal wage-and-hour law (the FLSA), Part 791 is reserved, not a declaration that joint-employer liability disappeared. The Department of Labor’s April 2026 publication is a proposal, not an effective rule or franchise exemption. Governing court law and the actual employment facts remain relevant.

Older disputes can have their own court-directed history. In its 23 February 2026 Browning-Ferris remand decision, the National Labor Relations Board applied the clarified earlier standard only as the law governing that case and expressly said it did not apply to cases arising after the 2020 rule took effect. Do not lift that older dispute’s test into a new arrangement without checking which law and period are involved.

practicalOutput: Check shared-worker hours and actual employment decisions before treating two payrolls as two independent wage obligations.
limitations: This makes no joint-employer finding or full governing-court, bargaining-unit or state-law determination. The named 2026 Board decision is read for its explicit case/time limitation, not as a complete current appellate-docket survey.
learningSummary: If businesses share people or employment decisions, separate incorporation and payroll do not by themselves settle responsibility. The wage-law and labour-relations tests must be kept distinct.

title: An import certificate does not close a later safety complaint
description: Certification and reporting serious new safety information are different responsibilities.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify the product and responsible certifier
paragraphs: The Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) scope and exclusions depend on the actual article, ordinary users, intended use and other agencies involved. A B2B invoice does not itself remove a product from that inquiry.

For covered imported finished products, Part 1110 defines the importer/certifier role, certificate contents and eFiling. Specified broker, owner, purchaser or consignee allocations are possible, but the identified certifier remains legally responsible for validity, accuracy, completeness and availability. The testing basis must match the actual applicable rules; a bought template is not proof. Keep the certificate and specified supporting records for at least five years from the certificate’s creation date, and meet the separate access and furnishing requirements.

sections.heading: An overheating report needs its own assessment
paragraphs: In a fictional example, a brand receives overheating information after assembling its import certificate file. The old certificate is not a reason to ignore the new facts.

Covered firms can have an immediate reporting duty when information reasonably supports the specified noncompliance, a potentially substantial product hazard or an unreasonable serious-injury/death risk. The rule interprets immediate as 24 hours, with its weekend/holiday computation. Do not wait for a complete risk estimate by default: a reasonable investigation is not automatic permission to delay once reportable information is known. A supplier’s promise to handle it does not settle every other party’s duty.

sections.heading: eFiling policy does not waive safety duties
paragraphs: The final action uses July 8, 2026 for most covered products and January 8, 2027 for specified foreign-trade-zone entries. The reviewed FAQ describes an initial policy against entry denial solely for missing eFiling data while certificate enforcement continues. That time-sensitive policy is not an exemption or guaranteed entry result.

practicalOutput: Bring new safety information promptly into the reporting assessment instead of treating the certificate as the end of the issue.
limitations: No product jurisdiction, technical test, reportable-defect, recall or shipment-clearance conclusion is made. The example does not decide whether its complaint is reportable.
learningSummary: A certificate concerns the applicable product requirements. New information about a hazard can create a separate reporting question even when a certificate is already on file.

title: Does overseas system access fall within the DOJ data programme?
description: The rule concerns defined people, data and transactions, not every overseas login.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Who receives access?
paragraphs: Identify the U.S. person providing access as well as the foreign recipient, data and agreement.
Part 202 can reach reading, viewing, editing or otherwise receiving data through a system or cloud platform. A foreign address alone does not establish a prohibited transaction.

Apply the actual covered-person and countries-of-concern definitions, including relevant ownership, organisation, employment, primary residence and designation. The recorded list names China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela, with China’s stated Hong Kong/Macau scope. Citizenship or an OFAC name result is not the complete test; an unlisted entity can qualify.

sections.heading: The data and count matter
paragraphs: Government-related data has specified regardless-of-volume criteria. Bulk sensitive U.S. personal data uses the following more-than thresholds under the category conditions. Aggregate over the preceding 12 months with the prescribed same-party rules; a new invoice does not restart the count. Mixed datasets have their own rule.

headers: Bulk threshold under the category conditions

sections.heading: What arrangement gives the access?
paragraphs: Data brokerage and specified human-omic transactions have prohibitions. Relevant vendor, employment and investment transactions can be restricted, subject to actual security and other conditions, including the required diligence programme and annual audit.

The corporate-group administrative/ancillary exemption is bounded. An independent franchise or licence partner is not automatically a subsidiary or affiliate. Prescribed security requirements cannot simply be replaced with controls the business regards as equivalent.

sections.heading: A restricted transaction needs controls at two levels
paragraphs: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) requires organizational and covered-system controls, plus a combination of data safeguards that fully and effectively prevents covered persons or countries of concern accessing covered data that is linkable, identifiable, unencrypted or decryptable using commonly available technology. Masking names can be insufficient if the recipient can reconnect records using other data.

The six-page requirements include monthly IT-asset inventory updates, remediation of known exploited vulnerabilities in internet-facing systems within 45 calendar days (with compensating requirements if patching is infeasible), and access/security logs stored centrally for at least 12 months. They require multifactor authentication; where technically infeasible or not enforced, passwords must have sufficient strength, including at least 15 characters.

Choose and justify the data safeguards through an internal risk assessment. The encryption option covers transit and storage: keys must not be co-located with the data, stored in a country of concern or accessible to covered persons. These are examples, not the full control list. Applying a security control does not turn a prohibited transaction into a permitted restricted transaction.

sections.heading: The earlier grace policy has ended
paragraphs: The programme began April 8, 2025. The cited operative diligence/audit provisions use October 6, 2025; the Department of Justice (DOJ) overview’s October 5 wording is the recorded source difference. The old good-faith enforcement-priority period ended July 8, 2025 and is not continuing grace.

practicalOutput: Establish the actual recipient, accessible data and transaction before assuming the helpdesk account is permitted or exempt.
limitations: These thresholds are not a general privacy safe harbour. No exemption, access authorisation or security attestation is supplied; origin-country, sector and other privacy duties remain separate.
learningSummary: A U.S. server does not remove the question if a foreign user can read or edit the data. Check the actual recipient, data and transaction first. For a restricted transaction, the CISA requirements now reviewed impose both system controls and effective data safeguards; this page does not certify a particular arrangement.

title: Minnesota franchise relationships: termination, nonrenewal and transfer
description: Termination, nonrenewal and transfer each have different cause, notice and evidence questions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review
practicalOutput: Identify whether you propose early termination, nonrenewal or a transfer decision before selecting a notice period or assessing money consequences.
limitations: Limited to the stated franchise/classification scope of section 80C.14. Going-concern valuation, complete Commissioner rules, sector, bankruptcy and judicial analysis are not supplied.

sections.heading: Identify the covered relationship and intended action
paragraphs: Start with the franchise definition in section 80C.01. Some franchise categories specifically recognised by the Commissioner receive different treatment under section 80C.14 subdivisions 1–2; check that coverage before applying the termination and nonrenewal rules below. Registration expiry is separate from the operator agreement’s expiry.

For example, if a brand wants the premises for its own operation when a weak-performing operator’s term ends, the actual purpose matters. The nonrenewal provision prohibits refusal for that conversion purpose.

sections.heading: Use the branch for the actual decision
paragraphs: The conditions below do not establish cause, value or an entitlement to approve or reject any actual action. “Cure” means correcting the stated failure. A going concern is the business valued as a continuing operation, rather than only its separate assets or initial fee.

rows: Good cause; 90-day written notice stating all reasons and 60 days from receipt to correct, subject to separate immediate-effect exceptions. Examine material/reasonable obligations and actual correction.

Specified abandonment, business-related conviction and prescribed uncured goodwill-default branch have separate conditions. The goodwill branch itself requires the prescribed prior cure notice; a listed cause is not automatically an immediate-notice exception.

Separate good-cause/failure-to-correct branches, or at least 180 days’ advance notice plus the stated opportunity to operate long enough to recover fair market value as a going concern, measured from failure to renew. This is not an automatic cash refund, compensation payment or return of the initial fee.

Consent may not be unreasonably withheld where the replacement meets the franchisor’s present qualifications and standards. Compare the actual buyer and reasons with those current standards; not every buyer must be approved.

title: Washington franchise exits: distinguish termination from nonrenewal
description: Work through cause, correction opportunities, territory and compensation without treating every exit as the same event.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Establish the state relationship and promised territory
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.010 uses the stated marketing-plan, brand and fee test, including oral/written and express/implied arrangements; required purchases/training and specified wholesale/property exclusions matter. Insurance and specified motor-vehicle treatment are separate. Neither “licence” nor federal classification decides it.

Section .180(2)(f) addresses competition and competitive grants where the agreement specifies an exclusive territory; it does not grant exclusivity to everyone. National accounts, online leads and actual service rights matter. Purchasing/conduct restrictions have separate reasonableness or business-ground tests.

sections.heading: Good cause and correction have distinct conditions
paragraphs: Section .180(2)(j) requires good cause for termination before expiry. Its ordinary default branch calls for written notice and a reasonable cure opportunity that need not exceed 30 days—not an unconditional minimum or automatic day-31 right.
If the problem cannot reasonably be cured in 30 days, the text separately addresses substantial and continuing corrective action initiated within that time.

The repeated-breach exception requires three willful and material breaches of the same term within twelve months, with specified prior notices/opportunities, then a subsequent willful and material breach of that same term within the same twelve months. Unrelated complaints do not establish it.
Adjudicated bankruptcy/insolvency, assignment for creditors, voluntary abandonment and the specified business-related criminal outcome have separate immediate-action conditions.

sections.heading: Nonrenewal has a different compensation rule
paragraphs: Section .180(2)(i) addresses fair compensation at expiry for listed assets bought from the franchisor and goodwill—the business value tied to established customer relationships and reputation—with exclusions and offsets. The goodwill exception requires both one year’s nonrenewal notice and a written agreement not to enforce a covenant restraining competition; it does not erase every listed asset obligation.
Good-cause termination has a narrower inventory/supplies purchase rule with a premises-retention qualification. Changing the action’s label does not establish the cheaper result.

practicalOutput: Identify the actual action and covered relationship before choosing a cure process or calculating expiry versus termination obligations.
limitations: No full damages, limitation, insolvency or litigation analysis is supplied. Section 190 remedies do not forecast an award; actual cause, compensation and exceptions remain conditional.
learningSummary: In Washington, early termination and nonrenewal at expiry have different conditions and money consequences. A reasonable cure opportunity is not automatic permission to terminate on day 31.

title: Wisconsin dealership exits: cause, advance notice and cure are different requirements
description: Understand why nonpayment does not automatically permit day-11 termination and why only specified marked inventory qualifies for repurchase.

sections.heading: Registration does not decide Chapter 135 coverage
paragraphs: Chapter 135 includes the stated in-state dealership rights to sell/distribute or use a commercial symbol, express/implied and oral/written, with community of interest. This concerns the parties’ shared financial interest in the business relationship; whether it exists depends on the actual arrangement.

Section 135.07 excludes specified motor-vehicle dealers/distributors/wholesalers acting in that capacity, insurance and door-to-door marketing; liquor has separate provisions. Actual operation, not a brand label or federal fee test, determines the inquiry.

sections.heading: Use separate notice and correction tracks
paragraphs: Section 135.03 requires good cause for covered termination, cancellation, nonrenewal and substantial competitive changes, with the grantor—the party granting the dealership rights—bearing the burden.

Specified insolvency, assignment for creditors or bankruptcy
Stated notice exceptions require the actual event and applicable conditions.

Section 135.06’s damages, costs/fees and injunction remedies have their own conditions; the provision is not an award prediction.

title: Virginia retail-franchise clauses after July 1, 2026
description: Learn the enacted retail-franchise scope, negotiated-sale exception and SCC amendment instructions before reusing an old agreement.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Apply the Act’s actual coverage
paragraphs: Chapters 553 and 554 took effect July 1, 2026. Section 13.1-559 requires the stated written retail marketing-plan/brand arrangement and a direct/indirect fee of $500 or more, subject to fee exclusions.

Performance must contemplate or require a defined Virginia place of business; incidental/ancillary and department exceptions have their actual statutory conditions. Calling an activity secondary does not alone establish one.

sections.heading: Review the two provisions separately
paragraphs: Section 13.1-559(D) requires Virginia law for franchise contracts offered/entered pursuant to the Act. Section 13.1-563(A)(4) prohibits offering/entering the stated restriction on franchisee retail offering, sale or distribution of goods/services after termination/expiry.

Section 563(B) permits the stated restriction when the franchisee sells to a third party or back to the franchisor at a mutually agreed price, for no more than two years after sale. Ordinary expiry or an unrelated payment does not establish that exception.
This is not a conclusion about confidentiality, intellectual-property or other distinct obligations.

sections.heading: A later sale may need amended documents first
paragraphs: The SCC’s April 14, 2026 notice calls for the language in the FDD (Franchise Disclosure Document) and agreement, through relevant Item 17 disclosure or a Virginia addendum.

For registrations begun before July 1 and expiring later, it distinguishes no expected Virginia sale before expiry from a possible/actual sale on or after July 1. The latter requires an amendment application first. A November offer using a pre-July template therefore cannot rely on registration age as proof of updated wording.

sections.heading: Clause updating is not an exit verdict
paragraphs: Section 13.1-564 separately restricts cancellation without reasonable cause and undue influence to surrender rights. Civil remedies and anti-waiver provisions have independent triggers; new wording does not decide an actual exit dispute.

practicalOutput: Check Act coverage, the actual clauses and planned sale date before using an older Virginia package.

learningSummary: Virginia’s July 1, 2026 retail-franchise changes address governing law and specified post-term retail competition. Earlier registration does not by itself update the documents used for a later covered sale.

title: Florida franchise and distributor claims: success, investment and market capacity
description: A separate statute can apply to particular franchise and distribution relationships even when a notice filing has been handled.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: First check this statute’s definition
paragraphs: The reviewed 2026 text requires its specified commercial relationship, granted offering/selling/distribution rights, an independent business within a distribution system, and substantial reliance on the franchisor for basic goods supply. It can include express/implied and oral/written arrangements.

Goods can include articles used or consumed in an approved service. Core chemical or equipment supply may therefore matter for a cleaning network; using a brand alone does not establish a pure advisory business is covered. Neither the federal franchise test nor section 559.802 notice replaces this definition.

sections.heading: Check what you say about success, costs and capacity
paragraphs: For a covered sale or establishment, section 817.416(2)(a) addresses intentional misrepresentation of prospects or chances of success, known required total investment, and efforts to establish more operators than the market or market area can reasonably sustain.

For example, two territories promoted as highly profitable might depend on the same customers. Compare the actual investment—including relevant omissions—and market information with what you say.
